newsitem.title: UK: VSNL GDR issue priced at 1,000 rupees. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: VSNL GDR issue priced at 1,000 rupees. [CORRECTED 11:35 GMT]

text.p: India's Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) said on Monday its global depositary receipt (GDR) issue had been priced at $13.93 per GDR, or 1,000 rupees per VSNL share (corrects to show that 1,000 rupee price refers to VSNL share and $13.93 price to GDR issue.)

It said in a statement the issue had been oversubscribed about 10 times. The price represents a 1.5 percent premium to VSNL's closing price of March 21 and each GDR represents half an ordinary VSNL share.
Gross proceeds from the offering, excluding an over-allotment option, amount to $448 million, making it India's largest international equity issue to date.
In the initial issue, 16.065 million shares have been sold with the provision for an issue of an extra 2.835 million upon exercise of the over-allotment option.
A decision on whether to exercise the option must be taken within 30 days.
The GDRs represent 13.19 percent of the company's enlarged equity share capital and the government's holding of 82.02 percent is reduced to 66.06 percent of the company's enlarged share capital.

"We are delighted with the success of the VSNL GDR issue. The demand from international investors has been outstanding and reflects VSNL's position as a global telecom service provider," VSNL chairman and managing director Brijendra Syngal said in a statement.
Trade in the issue started on Monday.
